beats.say: Your build robot has admin rights on the whole cluster.
One leaked token, and an attacker owns every namespace.
beats.label: The risk
beats.head: One token owns everything

beats.say: This port has two guards: access control, and pod security.
beats.label: Port 7 · Security

check.prompt: A new service account has no bindings. What can it do?
check.why: Access control only adds permissions. With no binding, a request is denied.

beats.say: First: who can do what, and where?
A role is a list of verbs on resources. For example: get and list pods.
beats.label: Role
beats.head: Verbs on resources

beats.say: A binding gives that role to a user or a service account.
beats.label: Binding
beats.head: A binding grants the role

beats.say: There is no deny rule. What you did not grant is denied.
beats.label: Default
beats.head: Not granted means denied

beats.say: Second: what may a container do?
By default, many images run as root. A break-out is then much worse.
beats.label: The default
beats.head: Root inside the container

beats.say: So run as a normal user, block privilege escalation, and drop capabilities.
beats.label: Harden the pod

beats.say: A label on the namespace makes the cluster reject pods that break these rules.
beats.label: Enforce it
beats.head: The namespace rejects bad pods

beats.say: Grant small roles. Nothing is allowed by default. And do not run as root.
beats.label: Security

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
